faqs.q: What is the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour. These rates are set by the Fair Work Commission and apply to award/agreement-free employees.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on an annual salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (the super guarantee rate for 2026–27). It is not deducted from your salary. For example, on an annual nba salary of $52,254.80, super would add $6,270.58, but only up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830.

faqs.q: Does the hourly-to-annual calculator account for overtime or penalties?
faqs.a: No. The calculator assumes the same hourly rate for every hour worked, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. It is a simple conversion based on hours per week × 52. For accurate pay, check your award or agreement using the Fair Work Ombudsman's Pay Calculator.

bodyMarkdown:
## From Hourly to Annual: Understanding Your NBA Salary

When you're offered an hourly rate or a salary, it helps to see the big picture. Converting an hourly wage to an annual nba salary is straightforward: multiply the hourly rate by the number of hours worked per week, then by 52 weeks. This guide uses the standard full-time week of 38 hours, as set by the Fair Work Commission. We'll also cover the National Minimum Wage, casual loading, superannuation, and tax so you can compare offers with confidence.

### How to Convert Hourly to Annual

The basic formula is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, the calculation becomes:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,254.80 per year

This is your gross annual nba salary before tax and super. If you work more or fewer hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. The [the timesheet](/) on this site lets you enter your base hourly rate and see the annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures instantly.

### Understanding the National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 ordinary hours. This rate applies to adult employees who are not covered by an award or agreement. Most employees, however, are covered by an industry or occupation award that sets higher minimum rates. For example, the Miscellaneous Award 2020 provides specific rates for apprentices and trainees. You can find your award rate using the [pay guides](/blog) or the Fair Work Ombudsman's online tools.

If you are a casual employee, you are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the minimum rate. That makes the casual National Minimum Wage $33.05 per hour. The [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how this affects your annual nba salary.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

When converting a casual hourly rate to an annual nba salary, remember that the loading is part of your base pay. For a casual earning $33.05 per hour (including loading), the annual gross is:

$33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,318.80

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee rate for 2026–27 is 12%. So on a $65,318.80 annual salary, your employer would contribute an extra $7,838.26 to your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional benefit. For more details, see [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. Using the National Minimum Wage example:

Weekly pay: $1,004.90
Fortnightly pay: $1,004.90 × 2 = $2,009.80

For a casual at $33.05 per hour:

Weekly pay: $1,256.90 (33.05 × 38)
Fortnightly pay: $2,513.80

Knowing your fortnightly amount helps with budgeting and comparing salary offers that are quoted per annum.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your annual nba salary is before tax. The Australian Taxation Office uses the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15c for each $1 over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30c for each $1 over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37c for each $1 over $135,000
- $190,001 and over: $51,370 plus 45c for each $1 over $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (based on 2025–26 thresholds for single taxpayers; the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this guide).

For a $52,254.80 annual nba salary:

Tax on $52,254.80: $4,020 + 0.30 × ($52,254.80 – $45,000) = $4,020 + $2,176.44 = $6,196.44
Medicare levy (2%): $1,045.10
Total deductions: $7,241.54
Take-home pay: $45,013.26 per year, or about $865.64 per week.

Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page for a detailed breakdown.

### Using the Timesheet

The [the timesheet](/) on this site is designed for quick conversions. Enter your base hourly rate (without casual loading) and select the casual loading checkbox if applicable. The tool will show your annual nba salary, weekly pay, fortnightly pay, estimated tax, and super. Remember, the results are estimates based on the assumptions listed in the disclaimer.

### Key Points to Remember

- Always use the correct hours per week. Full-time is typically 38 hours, but part-time or casual hours may vary.
- Award rates often include penalties and allowances that are not captured in a simple hourly-to-annual conversion.
- Super is paid on top of your ordinary time earnings, not deducted from your salary.
- Tax estimates are based on the resident scale and do not include HELP repayments, Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

For personalised advice, consult the Fair Work Ombudsman, the Australian Taxation Office, or a qualified accountant.
